summary: Add pool VLAN networks: a network is name + uplink NIC + VLAN ID; Core creates an additive per-VLAN guest bridge and persists it, the form offers observed NICs instead of free-text bridge names, and VMs pick networks by name. API impact: changed contract (POST /api/v1/networks kind vlan with uplink/vlan and derived source; NetworkRegistration and NIC.kind fields; network-register command semantics). Records the guest tools assessment in the plan. Also: automatic untagged default network per host bridge on a physical NIC, host-held pool state re-adopted by a replacement Controller (Inventory.guest_networks replaced by Inventory.managed with storage, networks, media and VM definitions from the Core journal; Controller adopts all four kinds with preserved IDs under actor system, request_id adopt-<kind>:<host>:<id>; Core resolves VM-create storage/network/media references by resource ID; nics[].master/parent), and a host Networking panel that shows physical NICs with what they carry. Enrollment with a different Controller now replaces the host identity in place (state and journal kept) so Add host works from a replacement Controller; report body cap raised to 16 MiB.

guide.reason: The network registration form changed from typed bridge names to a Connection/VLAN ID choice, with new prerequisites, refusal errors and switch-trunk troubleshooting. The Controller-rebuilt troubleshooting and a new "Replace a failed Controller" procedure describe what a replacement Controller recovers from each pool master and what it does not.

api.reason: Changed contract: kind vlan with uplink/vlan on network registration, derived bridge source, NIC kind in inventory, and additive bridge creation in the network-register command; both Controller and Core sides implemented with contract tests. Later the same day: Inventory.guest_networks/GuestNetwork replaced by Inventory.managed (ManagedState) so storage, networks, media and VM definitions are all adopted from the host journal.

state.reason: A pool network is a pool-scoped setting persisted on the pool master both as the registration and as the host bridge it creates.
state.record: network-register entry in the managed journal on the pool master (internal/vmhost, /var/lib/nex/core-local/vmhost/<operation-id>.json): the accepted command and its result are the durable record; the host reports them as Inventory.managed and a fresh Controller re-adopts them with the same IDs and names through adoptManaged. The Controller managed_resources rows are a mirror. The per-VLAN guest bridge itself persists in /etc/network/interfaces.d on the host and is reported as a NIC in inventory.

verification.method: go test -race ./... passed; Python contract/tool checks passed; installer network C test passed; TestGuestVLANNetns ran inside an unprivileged user+network namespace with sysfs remounted (dummy uplink; real VLAN device, bridge, ifupdown persistence and six refusals); simulated Chromium walkthrough registered VLAN 100 on the simulated host's nex1 and created a VM on it, captures inspected. Not run: native nested-KVM lab, physical NIC/switch trunking, Windows/Linux guest tools (assessed only). Controller adoption tests in internal/controller (TestHostReportedNetworksAreReadopted, TestDefaultUntaggedNetworkAutoRegistration) and the vmhost Applied() journal test cover automatic default-network creation, no duplication after failure, and adoption of host-reported storage, networks, media and VM definitions from Inventory.managed with preserved IDs. No Controller-replacement walkthrough against a real or nested-KVM host has run. The native lab harness tests/integration/vlan_lab.py was written but not executed; the fresh ISO lab reached the installer review page only. The main ISO in dist/ was rebuilt from this tree (0.1.0+vlan1 package and appliance). controller_replacement.py proved end-to-end recovery of a network across two real Controller processes in a network namespace; wired into both CI workflows. controller_replacement_debian.sh proved all four kinds (storage, network, ISO, VM) across two real Controllers with real libvirt/KVM; BUG-0039 fixed on the way. UI explanatory copy on the Networking tab and form was removed at Matt's request.
